masteryZone.q: Who is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution. He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly.

masteryZone.q: The Constituent Assembly of India was formed as a result of which plan?
masteryZone.sol: The Constituent Assembly was formed as a result of the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 proposed by the British government.

masteryZone.q: Who was the Permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the Permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly. He later became the first President of India (1950-1962).

masteryZone.q: Which of the following were members of the Constituent Assembly? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel were all members of the Constituent Assembly. Mahatma Gandhi was not a member.

masteryZone.q: The Muslim League initially supported the Constituent Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Muslim League initially boycotted the Constituent Assembly because they demanded a separate Pakistan.

masteryZone.q: Members of the Constituent Assembly were directly elected by the people.
masteryZone.sol: False. Members were elected indirectly by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies.

masteryZone.q: The Constituent Assembly first met on ______, 1946.
masteryZone.sol: The Constituent Assembly first met on December 9, 1946.

masteryZone.q: Total strength of the Constituent Assembly was ______ members.
masteryZone.sol: Total strength was 389 members (296 from British India, 93 from Princely States, and 4 from Chief Commissioners' provinces).

masteryZone.q: Who was the interim Chairman for the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. Sachidanand Sinha was the interim Chairman for the first meeting held on December 9, 1946.

masteryZone.q: Which plan led to the formation of the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: The Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 proposed by the British government led to the formation of the Constituent Assembly.

masteryZone.q: The Drafting Committee was chaired by:
masteryZone.sol: The Drafting Committee was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. It was formed on August 29, 1947.

masteryZone.q: Who chaired the Union Powers Committee?
masteryZone.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee which dealt with Centre-State relations.

masteryZone.q: The Steering Committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
masteryZone.sol: The Steering Committee was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad. It managed the day-to-day affairs of the Assembly.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following were important committees of the Constituent Assembly? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: The important committees were Drafting Committee, Union Powers Committee, Provincial Constitution Committee, and Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights.

masteryZone.q: The Drafting Committee consisted of 7 members.
masteryZone.sol: True. The Drafting Committee was formed on August 29, 1947 with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as Chairman and 7 members total.

masteryZone.q: The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
masteryZone.sol: False. The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

masteryZone.q: The Drafting Committee was formed on ______, 1947.
masteryZone.sol: The Drafting Committee was formed on August 29, 1947.

masteryZone.q: The Constituent Assembly formed ______ committees in total.
masteryZone.sol: The Constituent Assembly formed 13 committees in total to examine various aspects of the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: What was the main task of the Drafting Committee?
masteryZone.sol: The Drafting Committee was tasked with preparing the draft Constitution of India.

masteryZone.q: Who presented the Objective Resolution in the Constituent Assembly?
masteryZone.sol: Jawaharlal Nehru presented the Objective Resolution on December 13, 1946.

masteryZone.q: The Constitution of India was adopted on:
masteryZone.sol: The Constitution of India was adopted on November 26, 1949.

masteryZone.q: The Constitution of India came into force on:
masteryZone.sol: The Constitution of India came into force on January 26, 1950. This day is celebrated as Republic Day.

masteryZone.q: The original Constitution of India had how many articles?
masteryZone.sol: The original Constitution had 395 Articles, 8 Schedules, and 22 Parts.

masteryZone.q: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution is based on:
masteryZone.sol: The Preamble is based on the Objective Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are dates associated with the Constitution? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: December 9, 1946 (First meeting), November 26, 1949 (Adopted), January 26, 1950 (Came into force). August 15, 1947 is Independence Day.

masteryZone.q: The Indian Constitution is the longest written constitution in the world.
masteryZone.sol: True. The Indian Constitution is the longest written constitution in the world with 448 Articles, 27 Parts, and 12 Schedules currently.

masteryZone.q: Fundamental Rights are found in Part IV of the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: False. Fundamental Rights are found in Part III (Articles 14-32). Part IV contains Directive Principles of State Policy.

masteryZone.q: The Directive Principles of State Policy are found in Part ______.
masteryZone.sol: The Directive Principles of State Policy are found in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Fundamental Rights are found in Part ______ of the Constitution.
masteryZone.sol: Fundamental Rights are found in Part III (Articles 14-32) of the Indian Constitution.

masteryZone.q: What does 'Quasi-Federal' mean in the context of the Indian Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: Quasi-Federal means the Constitution has both federal (division of powers) and unitary (strong Centre) features.

masteryZone.q: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'Quasi-Federal'?
masteryZone.sol: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described the Indian Constitution as 'Quasi-Federal' because it has both federal and unitary features.

masteryZone.q: The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution deals with:
opts: Allocation of seats in Rajya Sabha
masteryZone.sol: The Fourth Schedule deals with the allocation of seats to States and Union Territories in the Rajya Sabha.

masteryZone.q: How long did the Constituent Assembly take to complete the Constitution?
masteryZone.sol: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days (Dec 9, 1946 to Nov 26, 1949) to complete the Constitution.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following are federal features of the Indian Constitution? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Division of powers, bicameral legislature, and independent judiciary are federal features. Single citizenship is a unitary feature.

masteryZone.q: Fundamental Rights can be suspended during a national Emergency.
masteryZone.sol: True. Fundamental Rights under Article 19 are automatically suspended when a national Emergency is proclaimed under Article 352.

masteryZone.q: Directive Principles of State Policy are enforceable by courts.
masteryZone.sol: False. Directive Principles are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts.

masteryZone.q: ______ is celebrated on January 26 every year in India.
masteryZone.sol: Republic Day is celebrated on January 26 every year to commemorate the day when the Constitution came into force (1950).

masteryZone.q: Constitution Day is celebrated on ______.
masteryZone.sol: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) is celebrated on November 26 to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution in 1949.

masteryZone.q: What is the Objective Resolution and who presented it?
masteryZone.sol: The Objective Resolution was presented by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946. It outlined the basic principles of the Constitution and later became the Preamble.

masteryZone.q: Name the first female member of the Constituent Assembly.
masteryZone.sol: Sarojini Naidu was the first woman President of the Constituent Assembly. The first woman member was Annie Mascarene.
